Self-caused bug, not a fork/subagent issue this time - discovered and fixed by the coordinator during stage 8 spot-checking. The coordinator's own earlier revert of q_1.1 (documented in the verify_correction_reverted entry) was run via the Bash tool as  with the intended Python string literal '
otin' (a single backslash + "notin") embedded inside a double-quoted shell argument. The shell's own quote/backslash handling silently consumed a layer of escaping before Python ever saw the string, so Python's parser interpreted the surviving '
' as an actual newline escape - corrupting the intended literal LaTeX macro '
otin' into a real newline character followed by the bare text 'otin' in q_1.1's part (iv) text. This propagated silently into 05_verify, 06_simplify and 07_format (each re-derived from the previous, corrupted file) and would have propagated into 08_tag's JSON if not caught. Caught via direct repr() inspection of the stage-8 JSON output during spot-checking (a plain print() of the text visually looked like the correct symbol, but repr() revealed the difference between an escaped literal backslash and an actual newline character). Verified the correct reading against 04_combined/combined.en.md (pristine, never touched by this correction) and confirmed it: '
otin', not a newline. Fixed via a proper .py script file executed directly (not through a Bash -c string), which avoids the shell-escaping layer entirely - replaced the exact corrupted sequence with the correct one in all 3 affected files, uniqueness-verified (exactly 1 occurrence each) before and after. Re-verified: mdio round-trip on 05_verify/06_simplify (100 items each), tag._parse on 07_format, protect.parity (06 vs 07, no drift). Re-ran the stage-8 serializer after the fix; the JSON now correctly shows the backslash-notin macro. Lesson for this session: never pass Python string literals containing backslashes through a Bash "python -c" double-quoted argument - write a .py file and execute it directly instead, exactly as this fix itself did.

A critical rendering bug was present in the design manifest entry above and its HTML all along, but only actually discovered during stage 10's PDF visual spot-check (checking pages beyond the first few, which happened not to show it) - stage 9's own numeric-read-back and figure-resolution checks could not have caught it, since neither exercises DOM structure. The converter's main character loop had no HTML-escaping for a bare "<"/">" encountered as a literal comparison operator in math content (e.g. "x<0" in a piecewise definition, "a<b" in an order-relation proof) - this chapter is inequality-heavy (57 raw </> characters across 06_simplify/chapter.simplified.en.md), and the first such unescaped "<" the browser reaches starts an unrecognized tag, corrupting the DOM for every element after it - visible on the exported PDF as every item from partway through the document onward rendering in a badly compressed, single narrow column instead of the normal two-column badge+content layout. Root-caused via repr()-level inspection of the raw HTML file (found the literal "x<0" sitting unescaped inside a <span>) before any attempt to patch symptoms. Fixed at the source: the converter's generic per-character fallback now escapes "<"/">" to "<"/">" (every other emission path already produces real, intentional tags via explicit string literals, so this cannot accidentally escape this stage's own markup). A second, unrelated markdown-syntax leak was also caught and fixed in the same pass: a literal "## Alternative Answer" heading marker embedded as solution text (q_1.10 part v, flagged but deliberately left untouched by stage 7's own report) was rendering as literal hash characters instead of plain text - stripped as recognized markdown-syntax noise, same precedent as the raw-image-markdown fix already applied earlier in this same design pass. Both fixes were made in the converter/render script, 09_design/final.en.html was regenerated and every stage-9 check re-run (figure resolution, command-coverage census, numeric read-back - all still pass), and 10_pdf/final.en.pdf was re-exported and its own gates re-run against the corrected file (see the pdf manifest entry immediately after this one - page count changed from the earlier, bug-affected 49 to a corrected 51, reflecting content now actually flowing at its intended width). The FIRST pdf manifest entry above (page_count: 49) reflects the bug-affected export and is superseded by the second (page_count: 51); the underlying PDF file on disk is now the corrected one only - the 49-page version was never a separate saved artifact, just an intermediate export later overwritten.
